apps.subtitle: Windows games on iPhone and iPad
apps.localizedDescription: A fast, controller-friendly launcher that runs Windows games on iOS and iPadOS with Steam and GOG built in, powered by Wine, FEX and Metal via DXMT.

versions.localizedDescription:
**BCD is in alpha:** an early stage of development, before beta. Many games run, many do not yet, and things can break between builds. When a game fails, please send a log.

This build brings everything since 0.1.623: new features, and two rounds of fixes from the logs you sent with Send Log and Report a problem and from Discord reports.

## New

- **Web pages from games and launchers:** when a game or launcher wants to open a web page (a sign-in such as Satisfactory's Epic login, a store link, a crash page), BCD now asks you first: **Open** (inside BCD, the game keeps running), **Open in Safari**, **Copy link** or **Not now**. Nothing opens without a tap. Before, such a page could not open at all, and Satisfactory's Epic sign-in failed with `EOS_UnexpectedError`. `env.MADEIRA_OPEN_URL = 0` in a game's config turns it off.
- **32-bit MFC:** a few 32-bit games and their plug-ins need Microsoft's 32-bit MFC (`mfc140u.dll`). **Settings › Visual C++ runtime › MFC, 32-bit** downloads Microsoft's 32-bit package (about 14 MB) and keeps only its four MFC DLLs. A game gets them when its config says `env.MADEIRA_MFC32 = 1`: What Lies in the Multiverse and Muv-Luv photonflowers have the line in their recommended settings, Auto-tune adds it after a start that fails for it, and the game's page says when the download is missing.
- **Send Log shows your code:** sending a log from **Settings › Logs** or a game's page now shows the code in a box with a **Copy code** button, as after a crash. When the newest log holds no game (BCD was opened again after the game), BCD offers the game's own log instead.
- **Game config saves on Back:** leaving the Game config page with Back, a controller's B button or the close button now keeps what you typed. Before, only Save did, and on an upright phone Save sat under the keyboard.
- **Direct3D 9 games:** BCD now refreshes only the part of a game's index buffer that a draw reads, instead of copying the whole buffer for every draw (Call of Duty: World at War copied about 0.9 GB a frame this way and fell to 32 FPS in heavy scenes). This is on for every Direct3D 9 game. If a Direct3D 9 game draws wrong with this build, `env.DXMT_D9_IB_RANGE = 0` in its config brings back the old way; please send a log.
- **Programs larger than the JIT pool:** a 64-bit program larger than BCD's whole JIT pool (METAL GEAR SOLID 4, Slay the Spire 2) now runs from its loaded file instead of failing to load. `env.MADEIRA_X64_IMAGE_NOCOPY_AUTO = 0` turns this off.
- **Helper memory (experimental):** `env.MADEIRA_POOL_MORE = 1` lets helper memory (Settings › Memory & performance) keep taking memory while the device has some to spare, instead of stopping at BCD's own memory warning. Off by default; Auto-tune offers it after iOS closed a game in that situation (Horizon Zero Dawn Remastered). From rtmtree's Persona 3 Reload fork.
- **Windows desktop:** console programs keep their window, a program opened from a right-click menu starts in its own folder, the desktop's first start on an install without games says how a game gets there, and the session line says when a program ended because it needs OpenGL or when the desktop's programs filled the JIT pool.

## Messages and hints

Text only; none of these changes a setting.

- **While a game runs:** a game that has been drawing for 45 seconds with no controller, no touch controls and no finger on the screen shows "No controller or touch controls are on. Open the menu and turn on Touch controls." (`env.MADEIRA_NO_INPUT_HINT = 0` turns it off). A game in a window with a title bar that is larger than the screen (a BCD Dock or Windows desktop start) gets one hint to choose Fullscreen or Borderless in its display settings (`env.MADEIRA_WINDOWED_HINT = 0` turns it off). The session line no longer runs under the menu button on an upright phone.
- **Before Play:** on a device that lets BCD use 4.5 GB or less, the page of a game of 8 GB or more says that iOS may close it and that BCD then tries a swap file. A Unity game's page says when the install lacks the increased memory limit, or when the device gives BCD too little address space for Unity's start. A 32-bit program that needs the 32-bit MFC says to download it first.
- **After a stop:** when the install lacks the increased memory limit, the stop message says so and how to add it. When BCD stopped while JIT was being set up for the game, the next start shows "The last start stopped early" with what to check in **Settings › JIT**. When you left BCD while a game was still starting and iOS closed it, the message says so instead of blaming memory. Exit messages name the library that failed to start (GRID 2: `steam_api.dll`), say when a program is larger than its executable window and which `exe-window-mb` to set (Hogwarts Legacy from Epic), say when a program looked for Steam, found none and closed, and say when the Wine server could not start.
- **Steam:** Home, the library and the end of setup say how to start a Steam game: open it, tap **Install**, then **Play**. Sign-in now says when Steam takes too long to answer (sign in to Steam again if it keeps happening) and when an install has no Keychain access (error -34018, a TrollStore install: install BCD with SideStore, AltStore or Sideloadly).
- **Storage:** Home says when very little space is left, and Auto-tune says when a game needs a swap file but the device has no room for one (Sekiro, Cloudpunk).
- **One-time installs:** when a game's installs are done, the screen counts down to the restart instead of looking like a crash.
- **Settings:** Frame generation now explains its cost and says to turn it off when a game runs below about 40 FPS without it (it can hold such a game at 20 FPS); the AVX switch says when a game needs it (a quit at start with an illegal instruction, or a message that the processor lacks AVX). **Settings › All settings** lists every new switch of this build.

## Fixes and improvements

> **Tried one of these games on an earlier build? Reset its settings first.** A game keeps the settings it had until you reset them, so without this it may start with the old ones that failed. On the game's page: **Options › Recommended settings › Reset to Recommended**, then check that **Options › Auto-tune › Auto-tune this game** is on, and start the game again.

Each fix targets the error a log showed; most could not be tested on a device yet, so a game may now get further and still stop at a later point. If it does, please send a new log: it names the next problem. "Known stop" means Auto-tune now names the stop and stops trying, instead of spending starts on settings that cannot help.

### Games

- **Age of Empires II: Definitive Edition:** its protection waits for a thread while it holds the program loader's lock, so the start stops after 45 seconds; a known stop for now.
- **Animal Well** ("black screen with sound"): its recommended settings log how bright the presented frames are, and the new no-input hint says when no controls are on.
- **Arctic Awakening and Supermarket Together:** Wine's `wintypes.dll` for their input plug-in (Arctic Awakening froze for a minute and closed through its crash reporter).
- **Assassin's Creed Rogue:** when an iOS start-up mapping already holds the address its program needs, Auto-tune says to close BCD completely and start again.
- **Batman: Arkham Knight and REANIMAL:** new recommended settings: 30 FPS and a tip to lower the graphics.
- **BeamNG.drive:** a memory call that made it crash on purpose now works; the game then stops at its browser part's second 32 GB request, a known stop.
- **BioShock 2 and other games in LiveContainer that sat on a black screen** (`bind: Operation not permitted` in the log): when iOS refuses Wine's server socket, the server now tries again from its own folder and otherwise carries on without it.
- **Blasphemous:** the game's own .NET exception is named, and its recommended settings log more of its own output.
- **Borderlands: Game of the Year Enhanced:** stopped at `cryptnet.dll` after loading more libraries than BCD's x86 translator kept track of (256); its recommended settings raise the limit. **Borderlands 3, Tales of Arise:** Unreal Engine's crash window now counts as a crash, so Auto-tune acts on it.
- **Call of Duty: Black Ops:** when `binkw32.dll` is not beside the program that was started, Auto-tune says so.
- **Control:** the crash 11 seconds in (`RtlRunOnceComplete`): new recommended settings and an Auto-tune line (`env.MADEIRA_KEYED_EVENT_PER_PROCESS = 1`) that Slay the Spire 2, Marvel's Spider-Man Remastered and Mechabellum get after the same crash; a launcher's game that crashes now counts as the session's crash.
- **Counter-Strike: Source (64-bit):** when its render thread waits for ever on a graphics query, Auto-tune gives the fix for queries that end in an empty submission, and the log says which query it waits for; `DXMT_D9_QUERY_LOST_MS` is a new opt-in answer for an occlusion query whose result never comes.
- **Cuphead and other BCD Dock games:** after you press Close, a game that ended cleanly now ends the session. A Dock game that closes by itself within 30 seconds, before it showed a picture (often after its own error box, as Yakuza 6 does), now ends the session too instead of leaving an empty desktop.
- **Cult of the Lamb, Kerbal Space Program, Mycopunk, R.E.P.O. and other Unity games that froze or stopped writing into their own code memory:** Auto-tune gives them the fix (`env.MADEIRA_MZ_VIEW_CHECK = 1`), and the recommended settings of Kerbal Space Program, Mycopunk and R.E.P.O. carry it. Mycopunk also gets Wine's `qwave.dll` for its Discord plug-in, whose failed loads filled the JIT pool.
- **Dark Souls III:** the crash from a texture view's level count (`env.MADEIRA_SRV_GETDESC_RESOLVE = 1`, from Auto-tune and the recommended settings).
- **Dead by Daylight:** the Easy Anti-Cheat error box is named also while it is still open.
- **Dead Rising:** a 5 ms audio buffer against choppy sound.
- **Dead Space (2023):** every first start ended after 5 seconds: its 419 MB program needs a larger executable window. Its new recommended settings give it one.
- **Diablo II: Resurrected:** its own protection layer stops the start; a known stop.
- **Euro Truck Simulator 2:** on devices under 10 GB its recommended settings skip the largest level of its compressed textures; when it is closed at the memory limit, Auto-tune goes on to the swap file even if you said it froze.
- **Fallout 4:** voices and music, which need Windows' WMA decoder. Copies of Fallout 4 and Skyrim Special Edition from outside Steam get it too. A session you played and then left now counts as played.
- **Fallout: New Vegas on 4 GB devices:** when iOS closes it at the memory limit while the swap file never filled, Auto-tune says the device has too little memory for it and which game settings help.
- **Far Cry 3:** its recommended settings log every registry entry its updater looks for and cannot find (the "Cannot find essential information in the registry" box).
- **Far Cry Primal and Watch Dogs 2:** their protection repeats a check thousands of times a second, which is too slow on a phone; a known stop, and Auto-tune no longer offers the setting that crashed the app for a Watch Dogs 2 player.
- **Farming Simulator 22 (Epic):** the game's process started without BCD's graphics handle table and never drew; fixed.
- **FINAL FANTASY RESONANCE demo:** its known stop in its own protection code is recognised in more logs.
- **FINAL FANTASY VII (Steam launcher):** the text of its error box and the sound system's warnings are now in the log, and Auto-tune suggests the game's own Steam launch option.
- **Forza Horizon 4 and other games that run for minutes without drawing:** named as known stops even when the session lasted long.
- **From the Darkness:** recommended settings against its 2 FPS (32-bit Unity code patching); `env.MADEIRA_WOW_UNITY_PLAIN = 1` is a new opt-in for other 32-bit Unity games.
- **Gal\*Gun 2 and Hello Neighbor:** stopped right after start inside OpenSSL's SHA code; their recommended settings hide the CPU's SHA extension from them (`env.MADEIRA_FEX_SHA = 0`).
- **Garry's Mod:** the stop at start in its browser part (8 of 8 logs, six devices): BCD's 32-bit layer read through an empty security answer; it now answers the way Windows does. A second 32-bit program started into a window an earlier one still held no longer ends the first one.
- **Ghost of Tsushima:** a helper program's error before the first frame no longer counts as a crash when the game then plays; a close at the memory limit goes on to the swap file.
- **Glyphica: Typing Survival:** the fix for its crash at start never reached the main `kernelbase.dll` of 0.1.600 to 0.1.623. It now ships as a separate copy that the game's recommended settings turn on.
- **GRID 2:** its `steam_api.dll` refuses to start; the exit message names it and Auto-tune names the stop.
- **GTA IV (Steam):** the Rockstar launcher's chain of programs gets more JIT pool room (recommended settings and Auto-tune), and a 32-bit window is allowed with 2 GB of address space left (Auto-tune).
- **GTA V and Red Dead Redemption 2 from Epic:** `env.MADEIRA_STEAM_IDENTITY = none` from the game's settings now takes effect (it was read too early), and Epic's GTA V starts the Windows services Rockstar's launcher installs.
- **GTA V Enhanced:** the crash in LiveContainer when BCD did not recognise its own code there; a freed block that fit is now used when copies of its libraries fill the JIT pool.
- **GTA V Legacy:** Auto-tune can keep BCD's code memory clear of the game's program address and tries a smaller pool margin when the pool ran out; after a GPU reset late in play it tells you which game settings to lower; when Social Club's helper runs out of address space it says to close BCD completely and start again.
- **Hogwarts Legacy:** the Epic version's program is 452 MB, larger than the 448 MB window of its recommended settings; they now give 512 MB.
- **Hotline Miami (GOG launcher) and other 32-bit programs started in a Wine desktop:** the crash at their first start. The launcher's "Updated" choice starts the OpenGL version of the game, which BCD cannot run yet; Auto-tune says to choose "Original".
- **Hotline Miami 2: Wrong Number and other 32-bit games without the Extended Virtual Addressing entitlement:** the placement 0.1.623 added for their smaller address space could still run out of room (Hotline Miami 2 then stopped at `d3dcompiler_43.dll`); BCD now also tries every free stretch the system reports, and the log says why a placement failed.
- **KINGDOM HEARTS HD 1.5+2.5 ReMIX:** its launcher stops in its own Direct3D 12 start-up; a known stop for now.
- **Kingdom Come: Deliverance (Steam):** after an update or a DLC, an empty folder whose name differed only in capital letters could hide the language packs. Steam downloads now keep the spelling already on the device.
- **METAL GEAR SOLID 4 (Master Collection):** new recommended settings. On devices under 10 GB, iOS closed the game while it loaded its textures (these GPUs cannot read their compressed format, and the expanded copies took about 1.5 GB); its recommended settings now skip the largest level of those textures there, and Auto-tune gives the same line after such a close.
- **METAL GEAR SOLID V: Ground Zeroes:** when its second copy failed to start, BCD stopped the whole session; now only that copy ends, and Auto-tune names the stop.
- **Metro 2033 Redux:** a memory jump of 1.5 GB in a third of a second before the first frame now counts as iOS closing the game (Auto-tune goes on to the swap file), and the log says what the jump was made of.
- **Minecraft Dungeons:** when BCD's x86 translator itself fails inside its own code, Auto-tune says it is a fault in BCD and the log names the place.
- **Need for Speed: Most Wanted and Underground 2:** their stops in the track loader are known stops; their recommended settings log the file reads and the code around the fault. **Need for Speed: Porsche Unleashed:** draws with Direct3D 7, which needs OpenGL; a known stop.
- **No More Room in Hell:** the 64-bit Source engine ran on Wine's Direct3D 9, which needs OpenGL; its recommended settings and Auto-tune give it BCD's Direct3D 9 for 64-bit games.
- **NW.js games (Game.exe):** their web engine could not load Windows' video decoders and stopped; their recommended settings and Auto-tune turn hardware video decoding off.
- **OpenGL-only games** (Battle Brothers, Darkest Dungeon, Noita, The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth, The Swapper, Dome Keeper and other Godot games that ask for OpenGL 3.3): named as known stops, since BCD has no OpenGL yet.
- **osu!:** an experiment with the CPU's memory-ordering options.
- **Outlast:** Auto-tune and the new recommended settings fix the start that stopped at `MSVCP100.dll failed to initialize`. **Outlast 2:** on phones with a 4 GB limit its recommended settings clamp the largest texture levels when memory runs low, and Auto-tune gives the stronger clamp after iOS closes the game.
- **Overlord and Overlord II:** the Overlord installer needs Microsoft's MFC 4.2, which BCD does not have (a known stop); Overlord II gets diagnostics for its configuration program.
- **Persona 3 Reload and installers that download (OpenAL):** only the first 64-bit program of a session got the root certificates, so a later one could not open a secure connection (Persona 3 Reload: "server not reachable"; the OpenAL installer: error 12157). Every program gets them now. Thanks to rtmtree, whose Persona 3 Reload fork found it.
- **Portal 2 and RoboCop: Rogue City (BCD Dock):** "Steam is not running" from a Dock game is a known stop that comes and goes. RoboCop: Rogue City also gets Wine's `dxva2.dll`.
- **PRAGMATA:** loads from its first start (new recommended settings). It then stops inside its own start-up code; a known stop for now.
- **Red Faction:** its setup found no video card on Wine's Direct3D 8; its recommended settings and Auto-tune give it Direct3D 8 through Direct3D 9.
- **Resident Evil 7:** a GPU reset during play is now named as such (it was taken for an audio problem), with the game settings to lower.
- **Rise of the Tomb Raider:** "Could not find any display mode" now counts as a failure, and its recommended settings and Auto-tune give BCD's monitor lines for it.
- **Satisfactory:** new recommended settings, and its Epic sign-in page opens (see Web pages above).
- **Schedule I and Dokimon Quest:** a controller experiment in their recommended settings (they see no controller today).
- **Slay the Spire 2:** its Direct3D 12 swap chain (DirectComposition) is served, and its recommended settings now also start its .NET runtime with write-xor-execute off and turn on the fix for an atomic instruction that 0.1.600 stopped at.
- **The First Berserker: Khazan:** its "Disable Mandatory ASLR" message is now explained: one of its program files must load at a fixed address below 4 GB, which iOS gives no program; a known stop.
- **Tales of Androgyny:** its launcher could not find its settings file; Auto-tune says to copy the complete game folder.
- **The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt:** on devices without room for its 32 GB memory reservation, its recommended settings and Auto-tune let BCD reserve half (an experiment; please send a log).
- **Ubisoft Connect, South Park: The Fractured But Whole and Assassin's Creed II:** they closed at start (code `0xdeadc0de`) because their protection layer runs an x86 instruction (`0x82`) that BCD's 32-bit translator did not know. It does now.
- **What Lies in the Multiverse and Muv-Luv photonflowers:** the 32-bit MFC (see New above).
- **WRC 9:** stopped after 32 frames, waiting for ever on a timing query. Its recommended settings now answer such a query after 2 seconds.
- **Yakuza 6: The Song of Life:** its start-up check says the CPU lacks AVX; Auto-tune now reports AVX to it (the emulation is slower).
- **Diagnostics only** (the next log names the cause; no setting is known yet): Deadpool, Doki Doki Literature Club, Fall Guys' installer, Friends vs Friends, Just Cause 3 (its GPU stall), LEGO Batman: The Videogame, lucieneslife, Mafia II, Requiem: Avenging Angel, Silent Hunter 3, Sonic Adventure DX and Unreal Gold (Auto-tune also no longer offers it a line that works only in 64-bit games).
- **Any copy:** the recommended settings of 25 games now apply to any copy of the game, not only to a Steam install: Batman: Arkham City GOTY, BlazBlue Entropy Effect, Borderlands 3, DARK SOULS III, Digimon Story Cyber Sleuth: Complete Edition, F1 2020, FINAL FANTASY TACTICS - The Ivalice Chronicles, FINAL FANTASY XV WINDOWS EDITION PLAYABLE DEMO, Jackal, Jetboard Joust, Life is Strange 2, Life is Strange Remastered, Lonely Mountains: Snow Riders, MARVEL Cosmic Invasion, PlateUp!, Project Zomboid, RAIDOU Remastered, Resident Evil 6, Resident Evil Requiem and its demo, Resident Evil Revelations 2, ROUNDS, SpiderHeck, Subnautica 2 and Yakuza: Like a Dragon.

### Launchers and stores

- **Battle.net:** its installer's browser now gets the same switches the launcher gets and its session splits the memory pool, so the installer no longer runs out of memory; a restarted 32-bit part no longer ends the session's other 32-bit programs.
- **EA app and Battle.net:** PunkBuster's services start only when a program asks for them, so the EA app's installer no longer finds every 32-bit memory window taken. When all of them are still held, BCD says to close the session and start again.
- **Epic:** when BCD Host stops before the game starts, BCD says so instead of asking you to sign in to Epic again. Epic's GTA V gets Windows services, and GTA V and Red Dead Redemption 2 from Epic get the Steam identity line (see Games).
- **Rockstar Launcher:** for error 113 from BCD Dock ("Steam is not running") the log now shows what the launcher saw of Steam, and Auto-tune tries two Dock experiments once. Rockstar's installer started by hand gets a plain message for its early error, and its own text files are in the log.
- **Steam:** the new start, sign-in and Keychain messages (see Messages above), and the folder spelling fix (Kingdom Come: Deliverance).

### Auto-tune

- **How it judges a start:** a game that crashed after its launcher ended cleanly is the session's crash; a freeze in BCD's own lock with no frame stays a freeze even if you closed it; a start-up memory jump that iOS ends counts as iOS closing the game; alive two minutes with only a few seconds of play counts as a freeze; a Rockstar Launcher error with no game frame counts as a failure; a session you played and left counts as played; a helper's error before the first frame is not a crash when the game then plays.
- **What it can change:** it can raise a recommended executable window when a crash proves it too small (Hogwarts Legacy from Epic); it sizes a swap file to the free storage; after a close at 95 % of the memory limit or more it goes to the swap file at once; it offers the experimental helper memory switch (see New).
- **What it says:** many new rules from your logs, with fixes or plain known-stop messages (listed per game above, plus: a game folder without `steam_api.dll`, a program library placed away from its program, an installer that needs MFC 4.2, a program that stops itself right after reading the processor's name, a device whose address space is too small for Unity, a GPU reset in any game). When it is stuck, the log says why each rule was passed over; it no longer shows Send Log after a verdict that only the install's memory entitlement can fix.

### Logs

New log lines for stops the logs could not explain yet, so the next log of such a game names its cause: the code bytes at a 32-bit trap and at an instruction BCD cannot run, the bytes at a fault outside every known code range (from rtmtree's fork), what a sudden memory jump is made of, the memory a bad jump points at and who created a thread that faults, each new process and a refused start in the Wine server, an early fault of the Wine server, failed registry requests (`env.MADEIRA_REG_TRACE = 1`), the text of an error box's details (`env.MADEIRA_WIN_TEXT = 1`), the texture formats a Direct3D 9 game creates, a graphics query that never completes (Direct3D 9 and 11), GPU stalls and slow-frame traces (opt-in), a 32-bit game's GPU time, the last debug texts of a program that ended on an unhandled exception, the start-up phase of a session that did not end cleanly, faults inside BCD's x86 translator, Steam's state when a Dock game cannot find it, the exact place of a 32-bit fault in the opt-in fault report, what a frozen game's threads and CPU were doing, Direct3D 12 calls that fail, who holds the address space a game could not get, the 32-bit Visual C++ runtime's start-up, and fewer repeated JIT pool lines.

### Under the hood

- 94 host checks that no build step ran before are now part of every build, with many new checks for this build's changes.
- The build refuses an IPA without BCD's Direct3D 11 changes in the 64-bit `d3d11.dll`, or without the opt-in DLLs a recommended setting names.
- Every recommended executable window is checked against the size of the programs in the test logs, so a too-small window fails the build.
- BCD's own `winebrowser.exe`, `kernelbase-optin.dll` and `dcomp-optin.dll` are built from source in the build; Microsoft's 32-bit Visual C++ package is downloaded only to check it during the build and is never shipped.

**Known issues:**
- Frame generation with MetalFX upscaling can make the graphics driver stop the game after a minute or two. Turn Frame generation off for now.
- GTA V and Red Dead Redemption 2 from Steam: the Rockstar Launcher sometimes says Steam is not running (error 113, "please reinstall") although it is. It comes and goes; fully close BCD and start the game again. If it keeps happening, send the game's log with **Report a problem** on its page.

Install help, game reports and ideas: join the [BCD-Games Discord](https://discord.gg/43TmupTVug).

**BCD.ipa**: the unsigned IPA, for sideloading with SideStore, AltStore or LiveContainer. It needs iOS 18 or later and JIT; the README has the details.
**BCD-source.tar.xz**: the complete source of this build with all its submodules (GPL-3.0).
